free_tier.stated: Free: 0 yuan, speed 0.5 Mbps, 20 concurrent connections, free domain, custom domain allowed, 2 TCP/UDP port numbers, unlimited traffic, daily check-in stacks duration. [translated]

egress.terms: Traffic is stated as unlimited on the free plan, with no byte counter named anywhere. The binding number is the speed: 0.5 Mbps sustained for 30 days is about 162 GB, so the plan cannot reach 1 TiB/month even at line rate.; ingress: udp

interface_detail: Windows, Linux, macOS and Android clients; http(s) domain proxying plus TCP and UDP port forwarding.
tooling: vendor client (3.5 MB, unpack and run) plus wg-quick on the local box
chaining: Two fixed UDP ports at 0.5 Mbps is enough for a WG control channel and a trickle, not for bulk transfer; pair it with a metered free VM for the volume.

limits.value: 20 concurrent connections on the free plan

binding_note: 0.5 Mbps is 5.27 GB/day at line rate, about 162 GB over 30 days, against the 3.24 Mbps that 1 TiB/month needs. Unlimited traffic is true and useless at this speed.

identity_cost.detail: The registration form asks for username, email, emailed verification code and password. No mobile number field and no real-name step appear on it.

reliability_note: Daily check-in adds time to the free mapping rather than traffic, so a free tunnel can expire; the vendor states it is a small operation with no guaranteed support.
confidence_note: Plan table and registration form both read first-party today. What would raise the rung is a probe measuring whether the 0.5 Mbps is per tunnel or per account, and whether the two assigned ports survive a reconnect.

evidence.proved: free plan is 0 yuan, 0.5 Mbps, 20 concurrent, 2 TCP/UDP ports, unlimited traffic
the service carries http(s) domain proxying plus TCP and UDP port forwarding
registration is username, email, emailed code, password

notes: The only provider that pairs UDP ingress with email-only registration, so it is the cheapest to test of the Chinese set. Whether the two TCP/UDP ports are fixed for the life of the mapping is not stated on the pages read. A licensed operator: the footer carries a value-added telecom licence and a domestic VPN service licence.

extras.wg_detail: The site describes a UDP proxy mode for reaching internal machines over UDP, and the free plan includes two TCP/UDP port numbers, so a WG datagram addressed to one of those public UDP ports reaches the local listener. No WG config is issued.
extras.volume_stated: Traffic is stated as unlimited on the free plan, with no byte counter named anywhere. The binding number is the speed: 0.5 Mbps sustained for 30 days is about 162 GB, so the plan cannot reach 1 TiB/month even at line rate.
extras.transit_note: Vendor relays on Alibaba Cloud, Tencent Cloud and older domestic datacentres.
